correctness.rationale: For the precisely labelled 4-cube, prove the fort duality, all-subset recurrence, upward-closure of forcing, and complete automorphism description. The fort algorithm checks each of 65536 masks (348 minimal forts: 28,32,288) while a separate direct synchronous forcing algorithm independently checks each mask (2360 minimal zero forcing sets, all size eight), and a third verifier checks all 65536 Boolean decisions for exact equality. The explicit five and eleven group-orbit representatives are tested against all 384 automorphisms and exhaust their respective sets. This is an exhaustive finite proof with standalone checked programs; it is not extrapolated to Q_d for other d.

originality.rationale: The retained claim is orbit-resolved structural classification, not the known scalar Z(Q4)=8 or known total 348 minimal forts. The 2025 closest full text explicitly states 348 in the conclusion but does not supply the two new orbit tables or well-forcedness, and states complete enumeration of minimum zero forcing sets remains unresolved. The 2023 thesis contains an exact probability plot for 16-vertex cube, mathematically encoding the polynomial, which is fully acknowledged rather than ignored. The novel conjunction of five and eleven orbit decompositions and well-forcedness is not implied by those covered scalar/probability results, nor by the 2018 zero-forcing polynomial framework. An unindexed source or dataset may still supersede the structural classification.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed labeled-set enumerations, unpublished program supplements, or graph-polynomial databases could contain complete orbit results; priority has not been independently settled.

value.rationale: The four-cube is the exceptional hypercube with two types of minimum forts and is explicitly the small open complete-structure test case in the 2025 primary paper. Resolving all five minimal-fort and eleven minimum-forcing orbits, including 288 large minimal forts, the uniform size-eight inclusion-minimality and propagation profile gives a natural complete classification rather than a gratuitous slice or only a recomputed aggregate. The five orbit generators form a compact exact obstruction certificate, useful for future hypercube and fort-transversal questions without asserting a downstream theorem.
